CATHERINE LAUTENBACHER.name: Catherine Lautenbacher
CATHERINE LAUTENBACHER.background: Dunwoody City Council member, District 1 Post 1, first elected in November 2021. Born in Italy to U.S. Navy parents; served four years on active duty as a U.S. Air Force intelligence officer (retired captain) with a C-130 unit in North Carolina. Holds an aerospace engineering degree from Boston University and an MBA from UNC Charlotte. Moved to Dunwoody in 2000 (Mill Glen subdivision); married to Conrad, two children. Former program director of Leadership Sandy Springs; works for Leadership Perimeter (2025). Past president of the Community Assistance Center, the Dunwoody Nature Center and the Mill Glen Swim and Tennis Club; board member of Discover Dunwoody; trustee of The Nature Conservancy's Georgia chapter. Re-elected unopposed on November 4, 2025, with 2,107 votes (100%).
CATHERINE LAUTENBACHER.record: Won the District 1 seat in 2021, defeating former council member Terry Nall about 53.6% to 46.2% (unofficial). On council she created the Dunwoody Nonprofit Roundtable, helped residents connect to DeKalb's water system to replace septic tanks, and worked on pedestrian crossings and walkability requests. Announced on June 16, 2025, that she would seek a second and final term. Took part in an October 22, 2025, candidate forum, where she said the council had voted yes on a senior housing project near the mall.
CATHERINE LAUTENBACHER.notes: Rough Draft (2021) says she had lived in Dunwoody 21 years; Appen Media says she moved there in 2000. Rough Draft (June 2025) notes Zach Humphries announced and then withdrew from the Post 1 race. Her 2021 race is outside the listed races but is cited from news for background. The campaign site in links is as named in Appen Media.

positions.stance: Local businesses create "vital economic activity for our city" and should be supported; in 2025 she said connectivity (trails, parks and road plans) "is the key to financial success for us, for economic development."
Wanted a program to "actively engage citizens in all aspects of civic service."

Supported investing in parks as recreation destinations (2021). In 2025 she did not recommend another parks and trails bond referendum, preferring to build parks gradually, finish Homecoming Park and then focus on Wildcat Park in her district.
Supported a social justice commission: "Focusing on equity is important for every community... We all benefit by bringing more diverse voices to the table."
Police benefits should be "commensurate with the value we place on them" to retain top talent (2021); in 2025 called for more proactive policing "beyond just getting drones."
Opposed a new Avalon-style development or added housing in Dunwoody Village; favored greenspace and unique concepts.
Agreed a special tax district could provide targeted money, including for police, and could lower other tax rates.
"We are, in general, for affordable housing. But it won't be easy." Pointed to comprehensive-plan transition areas such as Roberts Road for smaller single-family homes, duplexes or quadplexes.

statements.text: "I am happy to announce I'm running for reelection for a second and final term on this City Council."
On the council and Mayor Lynn Deutsch: "It's a good working group and I want to do one more term."
